haiku-low.q1: It is held 10 minutes (status HELD). If not claimed in time, it becomes EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale; the claim is then refused.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the customer is charged. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, Order marks REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, names the short items, and Payment is never contacted.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as an idempotency key. Payment retries with the same key, so the provider never charges twice.
haiku-low.q4: Order marks CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and requests a full refund. The order is not fulfilled; partial orders are never shipped.
haiku-low.q5: The cart is emptied only when OrderConfirmed is published after a successful claim. If checkout fails, the cart stays exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: Order coordinates each checkout and keeps the order's status, saved at each step. Its recovery loop repeats stuck reserve or claim calls.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which saves the outcome and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. Order consumes that event.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores each webhook event id in a unique processed table; repeats get 200 and no action. Handlers also check the current status before acting.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined. Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED and sends ReleaseHold, and Inventory releases the HELD hold so stock returns at once.
haiku-low.q10: The claim is refused if the hold is not HELD or the expiry time has passed, even before the sweeper runs. A refused claim leads to a full refund and cancellation.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is saved REQUESTED first, then moved to RETRYING with backoff retries using the same key. After N attempts it is REFUND_FAILED, alerts ops, and is retried daily, tracked in Payment.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after the claim succeeds, causes the Cart service to empty the cart.

sonnet.q1: 10 minutes (status HELD). If not claimed, the sweeper (every minute) marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale; it can also be RELEASED (e.g. on decline).
sonnet.q2: Reserved before the charge. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing (all lines held in one transaction or none), replies with the short items, Order marks REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK and tells the customer which items; Payment is never contacted and the cart is untouched.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key: the charge uses the order id as key, and retries reuse the same key, so the provider never charges twice.
sonnet.q4: The claim is refused. Order marks the order CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer and publishes RefundRequested; the customer gets a full refund (never partial orders).
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when OrderConfirmed is published (after the claim succeeds). On any failure the cart stays exactly as it was so the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: Order is the coordinator and the only service that tells others what to do next. The record is the order's saved status in Order's own database.
sonnet.q7: The provider calls the webhook on Payment; Payment saves the outcome and publishes a PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined event (via outbox) on the broker, which Order consumes.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores the provider's webhook event id in a unique processed-events table; a repeat finds it, replies 200 and does nothing (the unique constraint also covers simultaneous deliveries). Downstream, handlers check current status before acting, so repeated events have no extra effect.
sonnet.q9: The stock hold is released at once (status RELEASED, stock back on sale). Trigger: Order, on PaymentDeclined, marks PAYMENT_DECLINED and sends a ReleaseHold event to Inventory (which only releases a HELD hold).
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim the hold; the claim succeeds only if the hold is HELD and its expiry time has not passed. If refused (EXPIRED or past expiry), the order is cancelled and fully refunded, even if the stock is still unsold. Claim and expiry use a conditional status update so exactly one wins.
sonnet.q11: The refund row is saved REQUESTED before calling the provider; on failure or timeout it becomes RETRYING and a retry job repeats with backoff (stable key refund-order id prevents double refund). After N attempts it becomes REFUND_FAILED, raises an ops alert and is retried daily. It is tracked in Payment (refund row with status and attempt count); Order does not track it.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (published by Order after the claim succeeds) causes the Cart service to empty that cart.
